findings.F1: In falling calm markets, a coin's 3-day return grades its next 3 days: on the non-overlapping 3-day grid, the fallen third (3-day return about -4.6 % or worse) is followed by -1.46 % against drift (t -1.90, 61 cases) and the risen third by +1.84 % (t 2.15, 61 cases). The Spearman rho is 0.167 (p 0.024, 182 cases on 126 days). The pooled slope is 0.19, with an OLS t of 2.22 but only 1.66 when cases are clustered by day.
findings.F2: The grading holds across neighbouring choices but is weak on its own:
findings.F3: The short side alone, shorting the fallen third, earns +1.46 % per case over 3 days, about 5 times the 0.29 % cost of a trade, but its t with each day's cases taken together is only 1.57 over 48 days.
findings.F4: Outside falling calm markets the same 3-day grading is much weaker: rho 0.034 (p 0.26, 1,099 cases), with thirds at -0.53 % and +0.78 %. The short-horizon continuation is specific to the falling calm profile.

ideas.idea: In a falling, calm market, the more a coin has fallen over its last 3 days, the more it keeps falling over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: In an orderly decline, a trader would short the coins whose last few days fell hardest, scaled by the depth of that recent fall, and hold for a few days rather than one.
ideas.name: calm decline recent fall continuation
